message.content: {"skills": [{"category": "characterization", "trigger": "When evaluating a cystic lung lesion on chest radiography to distinguish intralobar pulmonary sequestration from other cavitary or cystic diseases.", "steps": ["Identify the location of the lesion, specifically checking for involvement of the lower lobes (particularly the left), which is the predominant site for intralobar sequestration.", "Assess the morphology of the cavity: look for a large, thin-walled cystic structure with sharp demarcation rather than thick, irregular walls or diffuse bilateral distribution.", "Check for the presence of an air-fluid level within the cavity, indicating fluid retention due to poor drainage and recurrent infection, a hallmark of sequestration.", "Distinguish from alternatives: reject diagnoses like bronchiectasis (typically upper lobe, irregular margins, no single large fluid-filled cyst), cystic fibrosis (bilateral, diffuse, thick-walled), or simple pneumonia (homogeneous consolidation without cavitation)."]}]}
